headline: MGS belly firms 1.6bp after a GDP beat and a Treasury rally; IRS swap spreads sink to one-year lows
summary: Malaysian government bonds firmed on Wednesday as Q3 GDP beat (5.5% against 5.3%) and Treasuries rallied overnight: on FAST's curve the 3Y slipped 0.4bp to 3.418%, the 5Y 1.6bp to 3.620% and the 10Y 1.2bp to 3.842%, while the 20Y rose 1.2bp. The 10Y GII fell 1.2bp to 3.880%, 3.8bp over MGS. Hong Leong Bank's IRS closes as of Nov 17 fell 1–6bp (5Y 3.59%, 10Y 3.80%), pushing the 5Y swap spread to −4.6bp and the 10Y to −5.4bp, both at or near one-year lows. FX-swap implied ringgit yields (Nov 18, indicative) were 2.89% at 3 months and 3.00% at 1 year, 6.6bp and 6.1bp under the onshore curve. FAST's AAA 5Y curve did not move, so its spread over MGS widened to 49bp, a one-year high, while government-guaranteed DanaInfra paper traded 22–39bp over MGS.
drivers: US Treasuries rallied on Tuesday as tech stocks slid before Nvidia's results: the 10Y fell about 2bp to 5.10% and the 2Y about 4bp to 4.79%; Nvidia then beat after the close. At the one-year daily beta of 0.15 that implies only −0.3bp for the 10Y MGS, which fell 1.2bp, so most of today's move was local. The KLCI still lost 0.5% to 1,566.7, its lowest close since August 2025.
GDP beat; BNM keeps a 2027 hike in play

Q3 GDP grew 5.5% against the 5.3% advance estimate (Q2: 6.0%), and Governor Abdul Rasheed said incoming growth and inflation data will decide any 2027 OPR move. The front end barely moved (2Y +1.0bp, 3Y −0.4bp) and the 3Y MGS sits 66.8bp over the 2.75% OPR, the 85th percentile of the past year; the RM5bn reopening of the 3Y MGS 3/29, announced on Nov 17, adds front-end supply.
IRS receiving pushes swap spreads negative

On Hong Leong Bank's Nov 17 snapshot the 5Y IRS fell 6bp to 3.59% and the 10Y 3bp to 3.80%; over a month they are down 16bp and 15bp while the 5Y and 10Y MGS fell only 2.3bp and 0.3bp. The 5Y swap spread (IRS − MGS) is −4.6bp (−5.1bp on the day, −14.4bp in a month), the lowest in a year, and the 10Y −5.4bp (6th percentile); the IRS 1s5s has inverted to −2bp. These are one bank's indicative closes.
Ringgit softer; FX swap cheap to onshore

BNM's reference rate put USD/MYR at 4.1055, 0.32% higher on the day and 1.29% on the week. The forward curve implies ringgit yields of 2.84% at 1 month, 2.89% at 3 months and 3.00% at 1 year, 9.0bp, 6.6bp and 6.1bp under the onshore T-bill/MGS curve: ringgit is cheaper to raise through the swap than onshore. Today is the first stored day, so there is no trend yet, and levels are indicative (FXEmpire forwards, US Treasury yields rather than SOFR).
data: A beat led by E&E exports and investment; it supports BNM's hawkish lean and caps how far the front end can rally.
Held with a firmer tone; markets price a possible 25bp hike in Q1 2027.
Weaker long-end demand at a higher yield keeps a supply premium in 15–20Y.
Strong activity data fed the GDP upgrade.
MGS +RM4.7bn to a record RM238.2bn (33.1%); GII −RM1.3bn (p n/a)
Foreign demand for MGS remains the anchor for the belly and the 10Y.
First rise in four months; gives BNM room to smooth the ringgit.
view: Stay modestly long the 5–7Y belly and neutral at 10Y: our 5Y call from Nov 17 (entry 3.636%) is 1.6bp in the money and stays open, and I expect the 10Y to hold a 3.78–3.90% range over the next two weeks. On the curve, keep 10s30s neutral until a long auction draws a better bid. The most stretched relative value is in swaps: the 5Y swap spread at −4.6bp (as of Nov 17) is the lowest of the year against a one-year average of +10.3bp, so I would pay 5Y IRS against a long 5Y MGS for a move back to +3bp, stop −12bp, accepting that the trend has run against it for a month. The FX swap prices ringgit 6–9bp under onshore rates and the 3M implied yield only 14bp over the OPR, so offshore money is not paying for an early hike while the 3Y MGS sits 67bp over the OPR; that makes the 3Y worth buying into the RM5bn reopening if it clears at 3.45% or higher. Close the Nov 17 'prefer MGS over GII' call: at 3.8bp the 10Y GII gap is near the top of its one-year range (average 1.0bp), so GII is the cheaper leg. In credit, government-guaranteed and Cagamas paper (38bp over MGS at 5Y) look better value than AAA corporates, and financial issuers have traded 83.5bp over MGS on average in the past five sessions against 47.7bp for SOEs. Treasuries explain little of the recent move (over four weeks +4.4bp of the 10Y MGS's −3.8bp), and the daily flow signal sits at −0.53 (sell-off), but its sell-off calls were right only 38.5% of the time since 2022 in an in-sample back-test, so I do not act on it.

buckets.name: Front end 3Y vs OPR

FX-swap implied 1M and 3M yields of 2.84% and 2.89% sit only 9–14bp over the OPR and 9.0bp / 6.6bp under onshore rates, so the swap market is not paying for an early hike. Nov 17 call (neutral, add near 3.55%): not triggered.
buckets.call: Buy the 3Y MGS 3/29 if the RM5bn reopening clears at 3.45% or above; target 3.35%, stop 3.55%.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y
buckets.why: The 5Y fell 1.6bp to 3.620% (78th percentile, one-year average 3.443%) and leads the curve this week (−2.3bp). The 5Y swap spread was −4.6bp on Nov 17, the lowest in a year (average +10.3bp), after the 5Y IRS fell 16bp in a month. Nov 17 overweight from 3.636%: open, +1.6bp.
buckets.call: Keep the overweight: target 3.55%, stop 3.72%. Swap-spread trade: pay 5Y IRS vs long 5Y MGS at −4.6bp, target +3bp, stop −12bp.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y is 3.842% (−1.2bp), the 78th percentile of the past year (average 3.668%, range 3.44–4.18%). It is 125.8bp under the US 10Y; the 10Y swap spread is −5.4bp (as of Nov 17, 6th percentile).
buckets.call: Buy at 3.90%, target 3.80%, stop 3.97%; no position in the middle of the range.

buckets.name: Long end 10s30s
buckets.why: 10s30s is 48.8bp (+1.1bp), the 65th percentile (average 46.9bp); the 20Y rose 1.2bp today. The GII 7/40 cleared at 4.158% with a 2.32x cover, so long-end demand is still soft. Nov 17 neutral call unchanged.
buckets.call: Neutral; switch to flatteners after a long auction draws a cover above 2.5x.

buckets.name: GII vs MGS 10Y
buckets.why: The 10Y GII at 3.880% is 3.8bp over MGS, the 91st percentile of the past year (average 1.0bp). Our Nov 17 call read the gap as tight; the one-year history says GII is the cheap leg, so that call is closed. The 10Y GII 7/36 traded RM300m today.
buckets.call: Prefer 10Y GII over MGS at 3.8bp; target 1.5bp, stop 6.5bp.

buckets.name: AAA credit 5Y
buckets.why: FAST's AAA 5Y is 4.114%, 49.4bp over MGS: a one-year high (average 28.0bp), up 5.9bp in a month. The curve has not moved for three sessions, so part of the widening is MGS rallying. Nov 17 trigger (55bp) not hit.
buckets.call: Add a first slice at about 49bp and the rest at 55bp; target 40bp, stop 62bp.

buckets.name: Cagamas 5Y vs MGS
buckets.why: Cagamas 5Y at 4.000% is 38.0bp over MGS, the top of its one-year range (average 22.5bp); Khazanah 5Y is 30.9bp over. Over five sessions, financial issuers traded 83.5bp over MGS on average and SOEs 47.7bp (DanaInfra 33.8bp across 14 trades).
buckets.call: Buy Cagamas 5Y at about 38bp; target 30bp, stop 46bp.

watch: Next: Malaysia October CPI (Nov 19; prior 1.8%), the RM5bn reopening of the 3Y MGS 3/29, the Fed minutes (Nov 18 US) and US jobless claims and Philadelphia Fed survey (Nov 19), with markets pricing a December Fed hike.
